newsitem.title: GERMANY: DBV-Winterthur sees good 97 life business.
newsitem.headline: DBV-Winterthur sees good 97 life business.

text.p: German insurer DBV Winterthur said on Wednesday it expected continued positive developments in its life insurance business in 1997 and double-digit new sales growth in the first quarter.
"We are expecting that things will continue to go well overall in 1997," DBV-Winterthur Lebensversicherungs AG chief executive Herbert Falk told a news conference.
New business in terms of policy sales and new premiums had double-digit growth rates in the first three months, he said.
According to preliminary data, the life insurance arm accounted for 2.6 billion marks of the DBV Winterthur group premiums of 5.5 billion marks in 1996.
DBV-Winterthur also announced plans to launch new life insurance products designed to supplement state pensions.
A new life policy linked to the German DAX blue chip share index would be launched in autumn, Falk said.
The company was also testing a new life insurance product at its Luxembourg subsidiary Winterthur Europe Vie which promised to double premiums paid over 12 years.
To data, around 50 such policies had been sold.
Falk forecast strong growth in coming years in corporate pension plans, and said it wanted to become a major player in this field within five years.
